lens.message:
Here's the shift: first-week onboarding is no longer ad-hoc wiki documentation — it's a mandatory standard. Wren Duskfield (Ops Lead): 'Every new hire completes the Pallasine checklist in their first week: accounts, pairing rotation, and a shadow shift. It replaced the old wiki page last quarter.' It changes our approach to how new hires get set up in week one, what the single source of truth for onboarding is, and how enablement and training get standardized instead of left ad-hoc.

Before/after — this shift currently lives in exactly one place, 'Onboarding Process: Pallasine Checklist':

As written: 'Every new hire completes the Pallasine checklist in their first week: accounts, pairing rotation, and a shadow shift. It replaced the old wiki page last quarter.'

As it reads now: the checklist is the governing standard for first-week readiness, not a newer page among many. The three components are required, completion is universal, and the old wiki page has no remaining role — replaced last quarter, not supplemented. Anything still sending new hires to the wiki is out of date.

Right lens?

Honest reach: no other documents came through with this conversation, so the list of what moves stops here — I won't pad it with maybes. If onboarding, HR, or training docs exist that this should also move, name them and I'll check it against those first. Want me to apply it across these documents once you do, or hold it as the standing read on this one?
